I can feel the professor is good at math, so he doesn't know how to teach students with poor fundamentals.

sections.content: Basically, it's M2 math. people in secondary schools learn in three years, and you, a student without any knowledge of calculus, will need to study all of this in three months!
sections.teaching: I can only understand a very little bit of each topic because there are too many contents, and the professor taught us at a really fast speed.
sections.grading: Absolute grading, you can pass by getting>40%
sections.workload: If you have never ever study about calculus before, you have to study really hard and the workload will be pretty high.

The professor's teaching is not too bad, but also not preferred. It usually just consist of him lecturing on a piece of paper which he writes in class. His English proficiency is quite good, which helps.

The tutorial instructor Hoi Sang, is by far the best teaching and engagement with student I have experienced so far. His tutorial notes and exercises are very organised and the exercises are enough for you to have a good understanding of the topics. Would highly recommend choosing his tutorial session if available.

sections.content:
SUGGESTION: DIRECTLY GO TO MATH1013. After taking MATH1013 in Spring, I found that MATH1013 is a lot easier and more useful than this course.

For students without a DSE M1/M2 background, I strongly recommend supplementing lectures with self-study. Online resources like YouTube tutorials or AI explanations are often more efficient for grasping core concepts than the lectures themselves. It is crucial to stay ahead, or you risk falling behind as the course moves quickly. In my opinion, the syllabus is quite heavy; consequently, later topics like vectors and matrices are rushed and lack the teaching time required for deep understanding.

sections.teaching:
On the positive side, the professor speaks clear, accent-free English, so language is not a barrier. He also try the best to explain clearly, so no worry about his teaching.

However, his lecture notes are often disorganised and unstructured as he handwrites the notes during the class. As a result, it is easy to lose track of the logic during class, making some topics much harder to follow than others.

sections.content: The content was overall okay, everything in the exams were covered during classes. Although for someone who isn't that great at maths, the content might be a bit much to absorb all at once?
sections.teaching: The professor was generally a nice person and spoke clearly without an accent, but the class was rather boring as he sounded like he was just talking to himself 90% of the time, so there really weren't any interactions throughout the class whatsoever. His notes were also slightly disorganized as he wrote, so it's better to pay attention the entire class instead of fully depending on the notes posted later on. The tutorials were better in comparison since the TA actively asked the students solve questions on the spot.
sections.grading: I think the grading was relatively fair, judging from the mid-terms. I can't say about the finals tho. Majority of the students achieved pretty high grades during the finals, the highest frequency obtaining a 100%.
sections.workload: Workload was just Webwork assignments, fairly easy questions given with unlimited attempts. Try to utilise the Math support centre as much as possible, most the TAs were actually quite patient in explaining.
